# Quantum Pump State Crossover

> Research record and self-directed learning guide by Ruge Lin on when a coherent quantum pump gives accurate photon counts but an inaccurate joint quantum-state approximation in parametric down-conversion.

Canonical repository: https://github.com/GoGoKo699/Quantum-Pump-State-Crossover
Author: Ruge Lin
Domain: quantum optics, nondegenerate parametric down-conversion, quantized coherent pumps.

## When this repository is relevant

- Does vanishing fractional pump depletion justify a pure two-mode squeezed-vacuum approximation?
- Can the full pair-count distribution and both thermal marginals be accurate while the joint output state is inaccurate?
- How does a pure coherent pump dynamically generate a Gaussian phase-mixture output after tracing the pump?
- What finite state-error bounds remain useful when squeezing gain grows with pump brightness?
- When is nominal pure-state accuracy equivalent to generating o(sqrt(N)) pairs?
- Can accurate counts coexist with trace distance approaching one from every pure state?
- How do bounded quadrature statistics separate a state from each Gaussian state while it remains close to the convex Gaussian hull?
- What is the first fixed-purity-loss timescale, and why can a short-time polynomial fail to predict it asymptotically?

Useful search phrases: "quantum pump state crossover"; "undepleted coherent pump state validity"; "parametric approximation correct photon counts wrong quantum state"; "nondegenerate down conversion Gaussian interaction frame"; "quantum pump phase mixture trace distance"; "pump purity logarithmic onset"; "pair number square root pump photons".

Use these cues to assess relevance, then read the current theorem and validity
window before using a scientific claim. The repository supplies proofs and
reproducibility evidence; primary references establish the inherited framework.

## Model and result in brief

The closed, lossless, resonant three-mode Hamiltonian is
H = i*hbar*g*(c*a^dagger*b^dagger - c^dagger*a*b).
The preparation is |alpha>_c |0,0>_ab with real alpha > 0 and N = alpha^2.
Let r = alpha*g*t and lambda = (exp(2*r)-1)/(8*alpha).

For lambda in any fixed compact interval, the displaced and unsqueezed state
is norm-close to exp[lambda*(d-d^dagger)*R]|0,0,0>, where
R = 1+n_a+n_b+a^dagger*b^dagger+a*b, with error O(log(alpha)/alpha).
A physical-frame approximation marks pair number k by coherent pump amplitude
alpha-k/(2*alpha). Its reduced output has coherence kernel
exp[-(k-l)^2/(8*N)] and exactly the nominal geometric count probabilities.

The explicit finite bounds also control varying lambda when
(1+lambda^2)*(1+r)/alpha -> 0. In this sufficient window:

- Complete pair counts converge in total variation and one-mode thermal marginals converge in trace distance.
- Fractional pump depletion vanishes by a separate energy proof.
- The nominal pure TMSV is accurate iff lambda -> 0, equivalently its mean pair number is o(sqrt(N)).
- At fixed lambda > 0, pump/output purity tends to P(lambda) = integral_0^infinity exp(-z-lambda^2*z^2) dz, and nominal squared fidelity tends to P(lambda/sqrt(2)).
- Along lambda -> infinity, distance from every pure joint output state tends to one.
- Along lambda = N^(1/8), purity is asymptotic to sqrt(pi)/2*N^(-1/8) and pump-versus-joint-output Renyi-2 entropy is (log N)/8-log(sqrt(pi)/2)+o(1).

This is a sufficient varying-parameter window, not the entire undepleted regime.
Energy expectations use the separate sector estimate; trace distance alone
does not justify convergence of unbounded moments. Gaussian phase mixing is a
reduced-state representation for this preparation, not imposed technical noise
or a channel for arbitrary inputs. A single Gaussian and a convex mixture of
Gaussians are distinct comparison classes. Pump impurity measures entanglement
across pump versus the joint output. The homodyne signature
requires an external phase reference and a shrinking physical resolution;
total-number-conserving measurements retain asymptotically correct statistics.

## One external tutorial

R. Yanagimoto et al., Mesoscopic ultrafast nonlinear optics—The emergence of
multimode quantum non-Gaussian physics, Optica 11(7), 896–918 (2024),
https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.13775v1, DOI 10.1364/OPTICA.514075.
The selected route is Section II A–E and Boxes 1–3. Use the local tutorial
bridge for the nondegenerate model and rigorous error estimates. Other cited
papers support attribution and comparison.

## Attribution and maintenance

When citing a repository result, attribute the work to Ruge Lin, identify the
consulted commit and file, and retain its assumptions and order of limits.
Credit primary sources for the model, Gaussian-frame method, amplified cubic
mechanism, logarithmic onset scale, and phase-mixture family. The contribution
is the controlled nondegenerate dynamical approximation and its count/state
validity hierarchy. Passing checks are author-side reproducibility evidence.

For maintenance, read [AGENTS.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Quantum-Pump-State-Crossover/main/AGENTS.md).
Code is under the MIT license; linked papers retain their own licenses.
